mbm-2051.clue: I sign my name with the left shoe.
mbm-2051.quote: The first time I climbed outdoors I left one chalky shoe print in my notebook. I drew the ridge around it while I was still tied in at the base. Best signature in the book.

mbm-2052.clue: My youngest cousin picked the loudest thread.
mbm-2052.quote: I let everyone choose one color for a quilt of our family kitchen. The little one picked violet for the egg timer. It still makes me jump whenever I see that square.

mbm-2053.clue: Nobody dives for the last peach.
mbm-2053.quote: Our beach volleyball game pauses as soon as the fruit cart rings. Last summer the vendor served one ball over the net with his empty basket. We gave him first choice of peaches.

mbm-2054.clue: I can sing that chorus underwater, almost.
mbm-2054.quote: My brother couldn't remember the tune we sang as kids, so I hummed through a straw into my glass. By the third wobbly note he had the words. Lunch was very wet.

mbm-2055.clue: I saved the picture that went through the wash.
mbm-2055.quote: I forgot a print of the old pier in my jacket. The water curled the paper and faded the sea. Mum framed it in a shallow box. Looks more like that windy day now.

mbm-2056.clue: I visit the button under the portrait.
mbm-2056.quote: At the museum there's an old uniform below a painted portrait. In the picture the sitter's collar button is undone. On the real uniform I could see the loose thread where it had been.

mbm-2057.clue: The paddle blade kept my lunch appointment.
mbm-2057.quote: We stopped our raft beside running water and drank tea off an upturned paddle laid across two stones. I still use that picture to persuade people that river trips have table service.

mbm-2058.clue: I give the sun a little sister.
mbm-2058.quote: I cut two suns into a yellow papel picado banner, one just peeking over the edge. When the line sags in the middle, the little one appears to be catching up.

mbm-2059.clue: I didn't crop out the clothes peg.
mbm-2059.quote: My best portrait of my sister was clipped to the washing line to dry. I photographed the print on the line, with the peg and the evening sky, and that's the version she asked to keep.

mbm-2060.clue: I keep the campsite's third chair.
mbm-2060.quote: My friend and I always bring one extra folding chair. On our first trip we used it to dry a map. Last July the ranger stopped for tea and told us exactly when the fireflies would come out. The third chair earns its ride.

mbm-2061.quote: I stamped a ring of leaves into a leather book cover. Mum's thumb always rests on the unfinished one. It has gone shiny all by itself.

mbm-2062.clue: The old signal box is the color of tea.
mbm-2062.quote: I tried matching its paint in my train sketch and ran out of brown. My granddad dipped the corner of a napkin into his tea. It was the exact color.

mbm-2063.clue: The dance ends at the washing line.
mbm-2063.quote: I cut a line of tiny paper dancers for our yard. One end came loose and they seemed to turn all together. My sister caught it and gave them a proper bow.

mbm-2064.clue: I let the old names live in the lining.
mbm-2064.quote: I quilted a railway blanket from faded route maps. Station names on the hidden side have changed. When my uncle wants his old stop I turn the edge up and show it to him.

mbm-2065.clue: My last stroke is for the caretaker.
mbm-2065.quote: The pool caretaker always rolls the divider out just after my last lap. Yesterday I reached the wall and he slid me an honorary paper medal through the steam. It was a bus ticket on string.

mbm-2066.clue: The fence posts used to be sleeves.
mbm-2066.quote: I made Grandpa's allotment in patchwork. His blue shirts became rows of cabbages, the cuff seams became fence posts, and one old brown button sits where his dog used to nap.

mbm-2067.clue: I brought the mountain down on my mitten.
mbm-2067.quote: Fresh powder stuck to my ski mitten like a tiny ridge. I held it next to the real mountains while my friend took a picture. By the next turn I'd skied both away.

mbm-2068.clue: I run the little loop twice on Wednesdays.
mbm-2068.quote: The library's book return is halfway round the park. I bring one book for myself and one for Dad. I drop his in on the second lap and call it a relay.

mbm-2069.clue: The blue ball is supposed to land in the hat.
mbm-2069.quote: I used Grandad's hat to catch the last ball of my act. The wind gave it a turn and the ball landed in Grandad's hand instead. He hasn't let me change the ending since.

mbm-2070.clue: I start the watch where the milk tastes coldest.
mbm-2070.quote: The dairy window opens just as my morning run begins. I stopped for milk once, left my watch on the sill, and finished the loop by the sound of their delivery bell.

mbm-2071.clue: Look for the pair of blue handles.
mbm-2071.quote: I stitched a blanket covered in little doorways. My twin cousins picked the same blue button for each of theirs. At bedtime they can always find each other's room.

mbm-2072.clue: I can play the song with my elbows tucked in.
mbm-2072.quote: My sister and I once shared one narrow marimba at a festival. Every time our elbows met we cracked up. We still play that tune shoulder to shoulder even when there's plenty of room.

mbm-2073.quote: I made a hiking mecha for the club. Its backpack holds a folded scrap of a real trail map. My friend inspected the rockets, the feet, and then asked where we were going camping.

mbm-2074.clue: I brought the old ski back to the dock.
mbm-2074.quote: My uncle's first slalom ski was too battered for another run. We cleaned it and fixed it across two low posts as a bench. He sits there in the morning and calls out my turns to the gulls.

mbm-2075.clue: There's one island I only visit by sound.
mbm-2075.quote: Along the estuary the reeds hide a little island at high tide. I know I've passed it when the frogs start up on both sides of my kayak. I drift there and let them finish.
